The lawmaker representing Delta Central Senatorial District, Senator Ede Dafinone, has expressed condolences to the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, and the entire Okonjo family of Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom in Delta State over the death of their matriarch, Professor Kamene Okonjo, who died at the age of 96. In a personally signed condolence message, Dafinone described the late Professor Okonjo as a woman whose life was marked by scholarship, commitment to women’s empowerment and service to humanity, adding that her contributions would continue to inspire generations. He said her legacy of excellence, compassion and devotion to family would remain a source of inspiration, even as her death left a significant void among her loved ones and the wider community. “Mama lived a remarkable life of purpose and impact, distinguished by her contributions to scholarship, women’s empowerment and service to humanity,” Dafinone stated. He added that her enduring legacy would live on through the lives she touched and the values she upheld throughout her lifetime. The senator noted that although the family was grieving, the late professor’s accomplishments and impact on society would remain a lasting part of her legacy. On behalf of his family and the people of Delta Central Senatorial District, Dafinone prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased and divine strength for the bereaved family. “I pray that Almighty God grants her eternal rest and gives the family the strength and fortitude to bear this loss,” he said.
